title: Glass, ice and garnish
lead: The glass, the ice, the garnish and the method are part of the spec. Get them right every time.

sections.name: Glassware

lines.label: In short
lines.text: The glass matches how the drink is served.

know: Stemmed glasses are for drinks served up.
Rocks glasses hold drinks over ice.
Tall glasses hold drinks with soda.
Chill a stemmed glass before a drink goes in.

sections.name: Ice

lines.label: In short

Fresh Ice in the glass; the shaking ice is strained out.
Scoop only: never scoop ice with a glass.

sections.name: Garnish

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Guests smell a drink before they taste it.

know: Aroma first: the garnish is the first thing a guest smells.
Express a peel by squeezing it over the drink.
Wedge wheel and twist are different citrus cuts.
Tongs or picks: never bare hands.

sections.name: Shake, stir or build
know: Shake drinks with citrus, egg or cream.
Stir drinks that are all spirit, for a silky texture.
Build highballs right in the glass.
Soda goes in last, in the glass, never in the shaker.

read.bigIdea: The glass matches how the drink is served.
read.where: **Stemmed** glasses (coupe, Nick and Nora, martini) are for drinks served **up**: the stem keeps a warm hand off the cold drink. **Rocks** glasses hold drinks over ice. **Tall** glasses (highball, Collins) hold drinks with soda. **Chill** a stemmed glass before a drink goes in.

read.bigIdea: Ice chills the drink, and its water is part of the spec.
read.where: Shaking or stirring with ice **chills** the drink and **dilutes** it; that water is part of the recipe. The shaking ice is **strained out**: the glass gets **fresh ice**, or none if it’s served up. **Big cubes** melt slower. Use a **scoop**, never a glass. If glass breaks near the ice, **empty the bin**.

keyPoints.line: first: the garnish is the first thing a guest smells.
a peel by squeezing it over the drink.
wheel and twist are different citrus cuts.

read.bigIdea: Guests smell a drink before they taste it.
read.where: The garnish adds **aroma** and finishes the look. To **express** a peel, squeeze it skin-side down over the glass so its oils land on top. A **wedge** is cut from the side of the fruit, a **wheel** is a round slice, and a **twist** is a strip of peel. Handle garnish with **tongs or picks**.

read.where: **Shake** drinks with **citrus, egg or cream**, to mix and aerate them. **Stir** drinks that are **all spirit**, for a clear, silky drink. **Build** highballs right in the glass. Never shake **soda**: add it in the glass at the end.

facts.fact: Stemmed glasses (coupe, Nick and Nora, martini) are for drinks served up: the stem keeps a warm hand off the cold drink. Rocks glasses hold drinks over ice. Tall glasses (highball, Collins) hold drinks with soda. Chill a stemmed glass before a drink goes in.
facts.source: Our book: Cocktail Specs, drink pages and the Safety page in this app

facts.fact: Shaking or stirring with ice chills the drink and dilutes it; that water is part of the recipe. The shaking ice is strained out: the glass gets fresh ice, or none if it’s served up. Big cubes melt slower. Use a scoop, never a glass. If glass breaks near the ice, empty the bin.

The garnish adds aroma and finishes the look. To express a peel, squeeze it skin-side down over the glass so its oils land on top. A wedge is cut from the side of the fruit, a wheel is a round slice, and a twist is a strip of peel. Handle garnish with tongs or picks.

Shake drinks with citrus, egg or cream, to mix and aerate them. Stir drinks that are all spirit, for a clear, silky drink. Build highballs right in the glass. Never shake soda: add it in the glass at the end.
